note: Attacker-controlled owner-name length is decoded from the EX_UOWNER extra field of the RAR5 file header; the value is not constrained to OWNER_MAXNAMELEN before use.
When the archive-provided length exceeds the 256-byte buffer size (OWNER_MAXNAMELEN), control takes the branch that clamps name_len to 256 instead of rejecting the entry.

Root cause: the maximum owner name length is not properly enforced. name_len is clamped to OWNER_MAXNAMELEN (256) while the oversized archive data is still processed, so the NUL-terminator write below lands one byte past the 256-byte stack buffer.
Copies exactly 256 bytes of attacker-controlled data into the 256-byte stack buffer namebuf, filling every valid index 0..255.
Sink: writes the NUL terminator at index name_len == OWNER_MAXNAMELEN (256), one byte past the end of char namebuf[OWNER_MAXNAMELEN] - an out-of-bounds stack write.
